messages.content: How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?

function.name: calculate_vector_angle
function.description: Calculate the angle of a vector based on its X and Y components. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

X_component.description: The X component of the vector. This is a float type value.

Y_component.description: The Y component of the vector. This is a float type value.

use_degrees.description: If true, the result will be in degrees. If false, the result will be in radians. Default is false.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?" They want to find the angle of the force for a given momentum. We need to interpret what they mean. Possibly they have a momentum vector and want to find the angle of the force vector? Or maybe they want to find the angle between force and momentum? The question is ambiguous. But we can provide general guidance: Force is the time derivative of momentum: F = dp/dt. So if you know momentum as a function of time, differentiate to get force. Then compute angle of force vector relative to some axis using arctan2 or similar. Use the function calculate_vector_angle to compute angle from components. Provide example code. Also mention that if momentum is constant, force is zero. Provide steps: 1) Determine momentum components p_x, p_y. 2) Compute derivatives dp_x/dt, dp_y/dt to get force components. 3) Use arctan2 to find angle. Provide formula: angle = atan2(F_y, F_x). Use degrees if needed. Provide example: Suppose momentum vector (p_x, p_y) changes over time. Provide sample python code.

We should call the function calculate_vector_angle with X_component=F_x, Y_component=F_y, use_degrees=True. That returns angle. Provide explanation. Also mention that if momentum is known at discrete times, approximate derivative via finite difference. Provide caution about units.

Thus answer: Use F = dp/dt, then angle = arctan2(F_y, F_x). Provide example. Use function.
